In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the grey ceiling hypothesis provides a parsimonious explanation for why there are so few large-brained mammals, but so many large-brained birds.
the expensive brain hypothesis predicts a negative relationship between relative brain size (or, equivalently, relative lifespan) and rmax.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expensive brain hypothesis predicts that brainy animals will go extinct sooner than less brainy ones.
the evolution of large brains is a risky business, and that the risk is higher in species where mothers do all the parenting.
the evolution of large brain size has been strongly constrained by the trade-off between the costs of brain tissue production and maintenance and the benefits of enhanced cognitive abilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of large brains is a risky endeavour that may have constrained the evolution of large brain size among homeothermic mammals and birds.
the evolutionary costs of large brains are not only paid by individuals, but also by their species.
the brain is not only expensive, but it can also be a liability.
